newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Dini takes issue with Yugoslav opposition.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Dini takes issue with Yugoslav opposition.

text.p: Italy's Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said on Monday that Serbian opposition leader Vuk Draskovic recognised that the Belgrade government would not reverse its annulment of disputed local election results.
Dini angered Draskovic when he said after talks with both sides in Belgrade last week that a reinstatement of the November 17 polls "is not on the cards".
Dini has instead welcomed an invitation by Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to Europe's OSCE security forum to send a delegation to Belgrade to verify the elections.

The Italian Foreign Ministry said Dini had written to Draskovic to remind him that the idea of a foreign mission to "examine the evident manipulation of the election results" had been suggested by Draskovic at their meeting last week.

"By that he recognised the improbability that the Yugoslav government would accept of its own initiative the opposition request purely and simply to reinstate the November 17 results," a statement said.
Dini met Draskovic and other leaders of the Zajedno (Together) coalition as well as Milosevic in Belgrade.
Students, union members and Zajedno supporters on Monday the began a fifth week of protests, protesting for the 29th straight day in Belgrade in a face-off with the government.

The crisis has shaken Milosevic and gave the United States a fresh opportunity to fire a broadside at the weekend pressing him for democratic reform in Serbia in return for renewed access to capital on international finance markets.
